people.name: Daibo Liu

people.bio: Daibo Liu received his PhD from the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China in 2018 and joined Hunan University in 2019. His research interests include IoT security, wireless sensing, and edge computing. He has conducted research at Tsinghua University and the University of Wisconsin–Madison. He is a Senior Member of CCF.

motto_en: Sense the Physical World, Empower Intelligent Future
about: The Spatial Intelligence & Trusted Sensing Lab (SITS Lab) at Hunan University studies how intelligent systems acquire information, understand space, sense their surroundings, and make decisions in the physical world. Motivated by the development of Physical Intelligence, we pursue fundamental theory, enabling technologies, and system platforms. We aim to extend sensing beyond the boundaries of conventional vision and wireless communication by bringing together electromagnetic radiation (EMR), radio frequency (RF) signals, signals of opportunity, physiological signals, and multimodal environmental information.

Our research spans spatial intelligence, trusted sensing, intelligent health sensing, privacy and security, and intelligent sensing systems. Topics include electromagnetic and wireless sensing, indoor localization and navigation using signals of opportunity, physical-space privacy protection, hidden-device detection, vital-sign sensing, multimodal intelligent computing, and integrated sensing and communication. We connect sensing mechanisms with intelligent algorithms and system platforms.

Guided by “Sense the Physical World, Empower Intelligent Future,” we aim to build trusted sensing infrastructure for the real world and help bring artificial intelligence from digital environments into physical spaces. Our work seeks to support smart devices, robots, intelligent healthcare, smart cities, and future mobile communication, providing safe, reliable, and efficient sensing for embodied intelligence and environments shared by people and connected devices.
